claim.claim-text: 1. A method performed by a device having a plurality of sensor controllers (112b, 114b, 116b) and a master sensor controller, wherein each sensor controller of the plurality of sensor controllers (112b, 114b, 116b) is configured to implement a respective filter that is configured to generate a single output value from multiple input samples generated by a corresponding sensor of a plurality of sensors (102, 104, 106), the method comprising:

2. The method of claim 1, wherein each sensor controller of the plurality of sensor controllers (112b, 114b, 116b) comprises a programmable register space comprising a mode value indicating whether or not the sensor controller is a master sensor controller.
3. The method of claim 2, wherein the programmable register space comprises a sync mask that indicates which sensor controller to monitor for sync signals.
4. The method of any one of claims 2-3, wherein the programmable register space comprises an enable value indicating whether the sensor controller should generate output values.
5. The method of any one of claims 2-3, further comprising:

determining, by the master sensor controller, that the mode value for the master sensor controller indicates that the master sensor controller should be a non-master sensor controller; and in response, assuming (420) a role as a non-master sensor controller.

6. The method of claim 5, wherein assuming (420) the role as the non-master sensor controller comprises waiting to generate any output values until another sync signal is received from a new master sensor controller.
7. The method of claim 6, further comprising:

determining, by the non-master sensor controller, that the mode value for the non-master sensor controller indicates that the sensor controller should be a master sensor controller; and in response, assuming (415) a role as the master sensor controller.

8. A system comprising: a plurality of sensor controllers (112b, 114b, 116b) and a master sensor controller, wherein each sensor controller of the plurality of sensor controllers (112b, 114b, 116b) is configured to implement a respective filter that is configured to generate a single output value from multiple input samples generated by a corresponding sensor of a plurality of sensors (102, 104, 106), wherein a non-master sensor controller of the plurality of sensor controllers (112b, 114b, 116b) is configured to perform operations comprising:

9. The system of claim 8, wherein each sensor controller of the plurality of sensor controllers (112b, 114b, 116b) comprises a programmable register space comprising a mode value indicating whether or not the sensor controller is a master sensor controller.
10. The system of claim 9, wherein the programmable register space comprises a sync mask that indicates which sensor controller to monitor for sync signals.
11. The system of claim 9-10, wherein the programmable register space comprises an enable value indicating whether the sensor controller should generate output values.
12. The system of any one of claims 9-10, wherein the operations further comprise:

determining, by the master sensor controller, that the mode value for the master sensor controller indicates that the master sensor controller should be a non-master sensor controller; and in response, assuming (420) a role as the non-master sensor controller.

13. The system of claim 12, wherein assuming (420) the role as the non-master sensor controller comprises waiting to generate any output values until another sync signal is received from a new master sensor controller.
14. The system of claim 13, further comprising:

determining, by the non-master sensor controller, that the mode value for the non-master sensor controller indicates that the sensor controller should be a master sensor controller; and in response, assuming (415) a role as the master sensor controller.

15. The system of claim 8, wherein the plurality of sensors (102, 104, 106) include one or more of audio sensors, light sensors, or proximity sensors, and optionally wherein the plurality of sensors (102, 104, 106) include both audio sensors and light sensors.
